contributions.title: Close the 24 coordinate-kernel span-six pools by a 3+1 restriction
contributions.claim_excerpt:
## Change and mathematical scope

PR #5231 leaves 24 coordinate-kernel pools unresolved for eight rank-one calls at address span six. This scoped written proof excludes that orbit: the literal projectors and every interleaved coordinate projector preserve a coordinate 3+1 decomposition. Relations of the triple subword inject into the full two-dimensional relation space. PR #720's disjoint-subset lemma bounds the triple's rank sum by its calls; the singleton has the complementary budget. Total rank is at most eight, contradicting three invertible 3-by-3 targets. Both singleton-data and singleton-auxiliary cases are covered.

The predecessor lemma is cited, not independently reproved. Combined span-six closure additionally depends on #4119, #5075 and #5231. Span five, additional auxiliaries, native costs and new kappa remain outside scope.

## Task and overlap

User-selected #5231 handoff; refined bit-new-register-model scope, priority revision 7. Base: 13be6ac685845c1ff671f5d26e7166165abd998e. Head: fb607e2385980dd36cd4bfc53885cb2ffab5d5dc. Bounded live PR text searches found no overlapping closure; full Discussion pagination and arbitrary diffs were not searched.

## Validation

CPython 3.14.4 on macOS arm64: normal/optimized direct replay passes all 24 pools, 2,800 short formal words, seven inverse controls, model-boundary controls and a nine-call span-six positive control. The verifier authenticates three declared predecessor inputs. All five canonical source blob IDs were recomputed. Metadata validate(check_pins=False) passes in a local Git fixture. Seven published blobs
